title: Investigation of energy compensation after physical exercise in people with normal weight and people with overweight
summary:
The study examines how exercise affects energy expenditure and energy compensation in normal-weight and overweight people. An imbalance between energy intake and expenditure leads to obesity, which is associated with diseases such as cardiovascular disease and poorer health. Although physical activity is generally considered healthy, little is known about how exactly it affects overall energy metabolism. In many cases, exercise does not lead to weight loss, but to increased calorie intake or other compensations.

The aim of the study is to find out how people of normal weight and overweight respond to exercise and the associated energy compensation. 32 participants will be included, 16 normal-weight and 16 overweight people, with men and women equally represented in both groups. Energy expenditure will be measured by mobile calorimetry, and hormonal changes and lactate levels will be recorded through blood samples. 
The results of this study may help to increase the understanding of the relationship between exercise and energy compensation and to develop more specific recommendations for weight loss in the future.
conditions: In this study healthy male and female individuals are being included

interventions.name: The test subject is subjected to a training session on two consecutive days. Thermogenesis, hormones and lactate are measured before, during and after the session.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthy normal weight (BMI: 20-25 kg/m²) or healthy obese (BMI: >30 kg/m²) subjects, without secondary or other diseases
Exclusion criteria:
- known psychiatric, neurological or internal diseases
- taking medication
- nicotine or alcohol abuse
- unusual psychological stress situations
- disturbed sleep-wake rhythm
- competitive sports
- diets in the last 3 months
- blood donation in the last 4 weeks
- current participation in other studies
